final_protocol:
1. Set up a sterile work area with a tube rack containing microcentrifuge tubes labeled 1, 2, and 3, sterile pipette tips, and single-channel micropipettes.

2. Using a micropipette fitted with a sterile small-volume tip from the 20 µL tip box, transfer the visible pink liquid sample/reagent into microcentrifuge tube 1 and close the tube.

3. Using a fresh sterile tip, transfer the visible pink liquid sample/reagent into microcentrifuge tube 2 and close the tube.

4. Using a fresh sterile tip, transfer the visible pink liquid sample/reagent into microcentrifuge tube 3 and close the tube.

5. Place the prepared microcentrifuge tubes labeled 1, 2, and 3 upright in the tube rack.

6. Retrieve a labeled Petri dish containing pink agar/medium and bring it back to the bench.

7. Place the labeled Petri dish on the bench beside the rack of prepared microcentrifuge tubes.

8. Using a yellow-banded single-channel micropipette with a sterile tip, pipette liquid from an open prepared microcentrifuge tube.

9. Dispense the pipetted liquid onto the labeled agar plate.

10. Close the Petri dish and gently rotate/swirl the closed plate on the bench to distribute the applied liquid across the agar surface.
